policy: Coverage may not decrease. Each denominator is measured separately and never averaged into a single number, because a Rust percentage and a browser percentage count different things. `scripts/check-coverage-ratchet.rs` compares a fresh LCOV report against the floors below and fails the build on a decrease beyond the stated tolerance. Raising a floor is automatic: run the script with --update-baseline and commit the result. Lowering one is not: it additionally requires --justification "<reviewed reason>", which is recorded as `lowered_reason` so a reviewer sees, in the diff, that the decrease was a deliberate decision.

browser.label: Browser production JavaScript
browser.evidence: `npm run coverage:web` runs tests/web/**/*.test.mjs under `node --test --experimental-test-coverage`. The unbundled page scripts and the 24-module worker mirror are executed through `node:vm` with their real repository paths as the script filename, so V8 attributes coverage to the files the browser downloads. The generated bundles above are build output and are excluded; their sources are measured instead.

rust.label: Rust workspace
rust.evidence: `cargo llvm-cov --all-features --lcov` over the whole workspace, which is what the `coverage` job in .github/workflows/coverage.yml runs. The floor recorded here was measured from a full local run of that command; a handful of integration cases that need outbound network could not complete in the measuring sandbox, so a green CI run measures at or above this floor rather than below it.
